Concentration-round first-touch (triage seat): promoted `finding` → `pm:queue`, **Bug** (label `bug` — the script reads a variable set nowhere in the repo, and dev-setup branding silently never applies), size S. Check-first clause per the card's own note: establish whether PR #5658's shared in-flight promise makes the inline fetch redundant entirely — if yes, **deleting** the inline fetch is the fix (less code, one origin); only if the pre-boot timing is measurably load-bearing does the variable-injection repair apply. Either way the two paths end up reading one value.

Third sibling #5703 is in `packages/auth`.

**Tier basis.** No path-derived mandate. Content judgement: clause ② does not trip — dev-only config plumbing, no contract and no public surface. Size follows triage's `S`; tier at the default judgement档 because the ruling has a **branch** to decide, not a patch to apply.

**Premise re-verified on `origin/main` `d8afbe519`:**

- `index.html:49` — `const base = (window.__CONSOLE_SERVER_URL || '').replace(/\/+$/, '');` then `:50` `const url = base + '/api/v1/runtime/config';`
- `main.tsx:65` — `const SERVER_BASE = (import.meta.env.VITE_SERVER_URL || '').replace(/\/+$/, '');` (and `:20` uses the same env var for `AUTH_URL`)
- **`window.__CONSOLE_SERVER_URL` is set nowhere in the repository** — re-measure this rather than taking it from me, and control the zero with a term known to exist.

**⚠️ Triage's ruling is a CHECK-FIRST, not a patch — read this before writing anything:**

> Check-first clause per the card's own note: establish whether PR #5658's shared in-flight promise makes the inline fetch redundant entirely — if yes, **deleting** the inline fetch is the fix (less code, one origin); only if the pre-boot timing is measurably load-bearing does the variable-injection repair apply. Either way the two paths end up reading one value.

**#5658 has landed** — `0e05aac68 perf(console): share one in-flight GET instead of racing duplicates on boot`. So the question is live and answerable **today**, not hypothetical. `index.html:19-25` already carries comments #5658 left about *"the page's ONE `GET /api/v1/runtime/config`"* and the `runtime/config ×2` it measured — **read those before deciding**, they are the closest thing to a primary source on what the inline fetch is still for.

**Answer the branch with a measurement, not a preference.** If the pre-boot fetch is redundant, deleting it is the better fix on every axis (less code, one origin, one value). If pre-boot timing is genuinely load-bearing — early branding painting before React mounts — then the variable-injection repair applies and the deletion would regress a visible flash. ⛔ Do not pick the branch because one is easier to write; establish which, say how you established it, and implement that one.

**Bounded severity, so scope stays honest:** this is **dev-only**. Both spellings resolve to `''` in production builds (same-origin), which is why #5658's dedup works there. The user-visible cost is a dev setup pointing at a separate server via `VITE_SERVER_URL` whose early branding silently never applies while the inline fetch 404s against the Vite dev origin. ⛔ Do not widen this into a production-config refactor.

## ACCEPT (on merits) — PR #5732 · reviewer of record, `domain:ui` seat, round 19

⚠️ **On merits; landing held.** Gates by name at 02:20Z (PR started 02:15:37Z): 13 `success` + 3 `skipped` + **6 `in_progress`**. ⛔ Not flipped ready until 19 + 3 is verified.

### The check-first question had a false premise, and the dev found it rather than answering it

Triage asked whether #5658's shared in-flight promise makes the inline fetch **redundant**. The answer:

> **"'redundant' is the wrong direction. The inline script is the PRODUCER of the shared promise; `initRuntimeConfig()` is the JOINER."**

`sharedGetJson()` joins an entry that already exists and otherwise starts its own — **no mechanism lets a later caller serve an earlier one**. So the inline fetch cannot be redundant *to* the module path; the module path is downstream of it. Answering the question as posed would have produced a confidently wrong "yes".

**Deletion was then ruled out three ways, each sufficient alone:**

1. **It removes no request.** The existing suite already pins **one** request both with the pre-boot script and without it. So the axis "redundant" would live on shows no gain at all.
2. **It changes *when*.** The single remaining request moves from parse time to module-eval time, and `main.tsx` awaits it before `createRoot().render()` — **it would undo exactly the head start #5658 landed three days ago.**
3. **The regression would be visible, not subtle.** `index.html` ships a `title` element with **no text** and a favicon link with an **empty href**. The pre-boot script is the only thing filling either before React mounts. *"Not a subtle flash — the static default is empty, not a placeholder."*

**And it is honest about what it could not measure.** Browser paint timing was not measured directly (no browser in the container). It says so, and explains why it did not need to be: (2) and (3) each rule deletion out from shipped code and existing pinned tests. It also names the distinction I asked for — this is the **positively-established** branch, **not** the conservative fallback I authorised for the unmeasurable case.

### The card's consequence was milder than reality

The card says the inline fetch *"404s against the Vite dev origin."* Measured: `apps/console/vite.config.ts:709` proxies `/api` to `DEV_PROXY_TARGET || 'http://localhost:3000'`, so the inline request **is generally served** — by whichever server the proxy points at, **which need not be the one `VITE_SERVER_URL` names**. And `inflightGetKey()` keys on the **full URL**, so two spellings meant two keys and **the two callers never found each other**.

So the real defect is *"answered by possibly the wrong server, and the dedup silently broken"* — not a 404. Premise valid; consequence sharper. A 404 is loud; being served by the wrong origin is not.

### A production regression avoided, and it was the non-obvious half

Vite's `htmlEnvHook` substitutes **only when the variable is present**, and otherwise leaves the token **verbatim** — read out of vite@8.2.1's own dist rather than assumed: `if (key in env) return env[key]; else … return text`. **The ordinary production build is exactly the unset case.** Writing the token with no guard would have put a literal, unsubstituted token into the URL of every production page — **converting a dev-only defect into a production one.** The guard makes an unsubstituted token read as same-origin `''`, so it can never reach the URL as a path segment.

### ⚠️ Gate reasoning for an unusual surface — worth reading before anyone touches `index.html` again

**ESLint's population is `**/*.{ts,tsx}` and matches NO `.html`.** So `apps/console/index.html` — which ships in `dist` and carries two inline classic scripts that run in **every user's browser during parse** — carries no ESLint verdict at all. What actually covers it: `check:control-bytes` (whose workflow deliberately has no paths filter, making it the one gate that always sees the file) and the vitest suite that **extracts and executes its text**. That suite is the real gate on this file, **which is why the fix is pinned there** rather than in a unit test of a copy of the script.

**Reverse verification** reverted only the `index.html` read site and kept the tests: **4 failed / 6 passed**, the headline failures being `expected vi.fn() to be called 1 times, but got 2 times` — **the two-request split itself**, which is the defect stated as a measurement. The 6 pre-existing #5544 cases stayed green under the ablation, so this change does not disturb what that card pinned.

**Container-ops note worth keeping:** a raw `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/console^...' build` **bypasses turbo and rebuilds all 35 packages**, hitting the ~10-minute foreground cap (exit 143). The dev verified the cap had **not** left the shared lock held, re-scoped to the 11 packages actually missing a `dist`, and finished in 66s. The non-obvious part: the closure build is needed for **type-check** (tsconfig has no path mappings, so `@object-ui/*` resolves through `exports` to `dist`) but **not** for vitest (src aliases).

**#5733 filed as a question, not an assertion** — `check-changeset-presence.mjs:416` counts only a package's own `src/` subtree, so `apps/console/index.html` can change with no changeset required, confirmed by the gate's own summary on this very PR (3 files changed, 2 counted). It notes the `src/`-only scope is documented as deliberate for dependency bumps and that the header simply does not discuss HTML entry points. Correct register for a gate-scope question.

Landing blocked only on the by-name gate read.
